messages:
ara: ran the microbench + small eval sweep for Helios-13b (new internal name). putting a short summary here and a recommendation for product/GTN handoff.

ara: key numbers: p50 latency 115ms (chat, 32 tokens), p95 420ms. throughput 1200 tok/s per GPU on our baseline kernel. cost ~= $0.28 / 1k gen tokens (hosted config, int8 q).

ara: quality: for chat dialogs we see negligible BLEU/ROUGE change vs fp16 (<0.4% delta). for long-form summarization there is a ~1.6% ROUGE-L drop on our editorial slice with int8, and ~3.8% with aggressive int4.

sam: thanks — what's the failure mode for the summarization slice? hallucinations, cutoffs, style drift?

ara: mostly style drift + more omissions on multi-paragraph inputs. hallucination count didn't move much. the model truncates some reasoning chains more often at int4.

miriam: do we have latency vs batch-size tradeoffs? product cares about tail latency at small batch sizes.

ara: yep. quick table: batch=1 p95=420ms, batch=4 p95=210ms, batch=8 p95=160ms. for convo workloads we plan to keep batch<=2 to meet p95 SLA.

jonathan: unit econ thought: if we ship int8 default, we drop infra cost ~38% vs fp16. moving to int4 drops infra cost another ~20% but increases eval regressions and support risk. my preliminary rec: default int8 for hosted+dedi; allow opt-in int4 via feature flag for low-latency/high-throughput internal tiers only.

ara: +1 to that. also propose a routing rule: short-chat -> int4 (when user opts in for cheaper plan), long-form -> int8 by default, with canary fallback to fp16 on quality regressions.

sam: can you paste the routing config snippet we'll hand to infra?

ara: sure, here's a tiny example we tested: ```
routes:
  - match: { workload: "chat_short" }
    model_variant: "helios-13b-int4"
    fallback: "helios-13b-int8"
  - match: { workload: "long_form" }
    model_variant: "helios-13b-int8"
    fallback: "helios-13b-fp16"
```

miriam: what's the QA bar for allowing int4 to go GA? we can't accept >2% drop on any critical GTN slice.

ara: current int4 drop on some editorial slices is 3.8% which is above the bar. int8 is within the 2% window. suggested path: ship int8 GA, run a targeted tuning sweep (temp/penalty + small finetune quant-aware) to reduce int4 drop to <2% on critical slices before broad opt-in.

jonathan: cost projection for product: with adoption mix (60% chat_short, 30% long_form, 10% background batch) and int8 default we forecast monthly infra spend ~ $142k for an average 100M tokens/day workload. if 25% of chat_short opts into int4 that drops to ~$118k. numbers are rough but useful for GTN pricing.

sam: good to have those. can we get the exact eval artifacts (test prompts + scoring) for handoff?

ara: uploading the seed eval set to the eval bucket now, will ping when done. includes: conversational slice (2.5k), editorial long-form (1.2k), code-gen small (800), rerank tests (600).

devops-bot: deploy-queue update: helios-13b-int8 canary started on cluster-gamma at 1765432300, health checks passing. :white_check_mark:

miriam: once canary is stable let's run a quick A/B on the editorial slice to confirm ROUGE and hallucination metrics before enabling routing.

ara: agreed. action items: 1) infra will monitor canary (jonathan) 2) eval team will run A/B on editorial slice (miriam) 3) devex/doc to prepare opt-in flag + pricing note (sam). I'll follow up with the eval artifact link in this thread.

jonathan: ok, will also add a cost-dashboard tile for helio variants so PMs can see real-time token spend.

ara: thanks all — low-risk path: int8 GA + quantified int4 opt-in after targeted tuning. will post the artifact link in ~30m. :party_popper:
